title: Quarterly initiative: Dedicated pool scaling rhythm, surge response experiments, and cost-to-latency tradeoffs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Define and deliver a quarterly roadmap that reduces per-token serving cost variability while protecting P95 latency SLOs for Dedicated pools. We will run a set of controlled experiments (surge response, pre-inflate windows, and adaptive allocation) and ship guardrails + observability so product teams can opt into safer elasticity settings.

Background: Customers running steady but spiky workloads have asked for predictable economics without sacrificing latency. Previous efforts focused on large warm pools and blunt reservation hedges. Feedback: cost volatility remains during cross-region peaks and transient bursts, and current telemetry doesn't link allocation decisions to observed user latency or downstream error rate.

Approach: 1) Signal and policy: define a short decisive signal taxonomy (concurrency, tokens/s, queued-time) and three policy families (conservative, balanced, aggressive). 2) Experiments: build three isolated experiment lanes that exercise different allocation rhythms: (A) short-burst authoring (30s–5m), (B) sustained surge (10–60m), (C) slow ramp (hours). Each lane will include canaries, automatic rollback triggers, and a cost-to-latency dashboard. 3) Observability: instrument token-level cost attribution, per-route P95/P99 latency, and model-variant fallback counts. 4) Operational controls: add per-project allocation caps, emergency thaw/freeze, and a lightweight simulation mode in Console to preview economic outcomes.

Out of scope for this quarter: full reservation re-pricing, deep kernel/runtime kernel changes, or changes that require customers to change client code. Those will be tracked as follow-up initiatives.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Experiment lanes implemented and gated by feature flags.
- End-to-end dashboard that correlates allocation decisions with P95 and net cost delta for each experiment lane.
- One pilot customer (internal or early adopter) has run at least two weeks on the balanced policy with <10% cost variability and no >10% regressions in P95.
- Rollout playbook and rollback criteria documented in Console runbook.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: aggressive policies cause transient P99 spikes. Mitigation: immediate fallback to conservative policy and circuit-breaker alerts to SRE.
- Risk: telemetry misses cross-region effects. Mitigation: add end-to-end tracing hooks and a synthetic global traffic generator.
- Risk: cost metrics opaque to customers; Mitigation: include simple per-route cost preview in Console simulation.

Stakeholders: product (Ava Martinez, Liam Chen), runtime eng (ENG-4021 owner: Priya Singh), infra/slo (ENG-5143 owner: Marco Ruiz), Design (for simulation UI: Nina Patel), Solutions/Customer Success (pilot recruiting).

Notes and links: See design brief (Drive: /Shared/Dedicated/Scaling-Rhythm-v1), initial telemetry spike analysis (notebook link), and the canary checklist (Confluence: /runbooks/canary-surge).

No customer-facing regressions (errors or timeouts) caused by experiment policies
Deliver a Console simulation that predicts cost delta within +/-15% vs observed
